today.h: Yields Ease, Records Follow: the S&P Closes Above 7,800 for the First Time
today.c1: Monday's pressure valves opened Tuesday. The 10-year yield pulled back ~4bp to 5.27% from Monday's 24-year-high spike (5.349% intraday), global bonds rallied with it (Bunds -5bp, OATs -9bp, Italy -11bp), Brent slid below $98 in the morning as Gulf supply kept recovering, and the money that had been hiding went back to work: the S&P 500 closed above 7,800 for the first time (7,818.93, +0.58%), the Nasdaq set a second straight record close (27,599.79, +0.45%), and the Dow added 253 points (+0.49%) to 51,521.28 — still just over 5% below its Aug. 5 record. Ten of 11 sectors closed green, led by utilities (+3.0%) as Constellation Energy jumped 12% on a 20-year Google power deal (890MW of new nuclear plus a 2,700MW supply agreement, $4.3B of new Constellation investment). AI optimism returned in the names that pay for the buildout — Nvidia's third straight intraday record ($6T market cap in sight), AMD +2.8% on Citi's Street-high $800 target, Marvell +5.8% on raised guidance, Ciena +13.9% — while the memory trade broke: Seagate -9.2% and Western Digital -6.9% as Bloomberg reported a Seagate-Toshiba bidding war for TDK's magnetic-heads unit on top of Friday's Toshiba capacity shock. Small caps lagged (Russell 2000 -0.6%) and Health Care was the lone red sector (-0.2%; Moderna -7.8%, Novavax -9.9% gave back part of their runs). The tape's quiet tells: VIX -3.3% to 15.0, gold +0.7% to $4,187.10, the dollar -0.3% to 101.86, bitcoin -0.2% — and a trade deficit that widened to $105.6B in August (the widest since early 2025) as imports set a record. Next referee: September FOMC minutes, Wednesday 2 pm ET.
today.c4:
• Rates flipped from ceiling to fuel: Monday's 5.35% spike was bought, Tuesday's retreat was rewarded — the watch is whether 5.25-5.30% holds; FOMC minutes (Wed 2 pm) and CPI (Oct 14) referee next.
  • The dispersion trade sharpened: power and AI infrastructure got paid (Constellation's nuclear PPA, optics, neoclouds) while memory got sold (Seagate -9%) — own the bottleneck, not the commodity.
  • Oil's round trip (below $98 to a $100.58 settle) says the premium re-arms on every escalation headline — $100 Brent is still the inflation line, and diesel is still its tightest corner.

chains.t: ① Main Chain: Yields Retreat From 2002 Highs, and the Records Follow
steps: Overnight: global bonds rally — Bunds -5bp, OATs -9bp, Italy -11bp to 4.52% — taking the edge off Monday's 24-year-high yield spike
Morning: Brent slides below $98 (a session low just above $97) as Gulf supply recovers — the day's first pressure valve
US yields follow: the 10Y pulls back ~4bp to 5.27% (30Y -2bp to 5.64%); the dollar slips to 101.86 (-0.3%); VIX eases to 15.0 (-3.3%)
Risk appetite returns to the compounding names: Nvidia sets a third straight intraday record ($6T cap in sight), AMD +2.8% on Citi's Street-high $800 target, Marvell +5.8% on raised guidance
Records follow: S&P closes above 7,800 for the first time (7,818.93, +0.58%); Nasdaq another record (27,599.79, +0.45%); Dow +0.49% to 51,521.28
The day's emblem: Constellation Energy +12% on a 20-year Google nuclear-power deal
chains.d: One story explained Tuesday's 60%: the bond market's first real pause of October opened the pressure valves — oil dipped, yields eased, and the money that had been hiding went back to work in AI and into records.

news.fact: US stocks ended higher as crude prices steadied and Treasury yields eased, letting markets turn to the approaching third-quarter reporting season; the S&P 500 and Nasdaq reached record closing highs.
The S&P 500 closed above 7,800 for the first time — up 0.6% on the day — and the Nasdaq set another record close; the Dow remains just over 5% shy of its Aug. 5 record.
Treasury yields were lower as a surge to multi-decade highs took a pause; the event of the week is Wednesday's release of the September FOMC minutes.
Constellation Energy jumped 12.3% after Alphabet entered into a 3,590-megawatt power deal with the company.
Google will buy power tied to 890 megawatts of new nuclear capacity, alongside a separate 2,700-megawatt supply agreement, supporting more than $4.3 billion in new Constellation investment.
Nvidia shares set their third straight intraday record Tuesday before closing up 0.1%, as the company closed in on a $6 trillion market capitalization.
Oil prices ended the day little changed: Brent crude traded 0.26% higher to settle at $100.58 a barrel; WTI futures rose 0.01% to $89.44.

chains.t: ② The Split Tape: Power and AI Infrastructure Get Paid — Memory Gets Sold
steps: The bottleneck trades got paid: Ciena +13.9%, Astera Labs +7.6%, Nebius +7.4%, CoreWeave +5.0% — enthusiasm returned to AI-buildout names
The Google deal's fine print: 890MW of new nuclear plus a 2,700MW supply agreement — more than $4.3B of new Constellation investment; Alphabet +0.4%
Semis vs storage: the SOX +0.3% while the HDD corner broke — the split ran through the whole stack
Memory's wipeout: Seagate -9.2%, Western Digital -6.9%, SK Hynix -6.4%, the memory ETF (DRAM) -3.5%, SanDisk -2.6%
The trigger: Bloomberg reports Seagate and Toshiba are bidding for TDK's magnetic-heads unit — colliding with Friday's Toshiba capacity-doubling shock; Wedbush doubts the deal could clear antitrust
The edges: Moderna -7.8% and Novavax -9.9% gave back part of their runs; Option Care Health +33% on its $5.8B takeout
chains.d: Under the records sat a clean split: the AI buildout's bottlenecks — power, optics, custom silicon — got paid by the billion, while its commodities got sold on a supply scare.

news.fact: AI-buildout stocks surged as enthusiasm returned — Ciena jumped 11.3%, Nebius Group climbed 9.5%, Astera Labs 7.5% and CoreWeave 4% — while memory names slid as investors reassessed the outlook for demand and profits stemming from the data-center boom.

Seagate and Western Digital fell as investors assessed Toshiba's potential HDD expansion and a Bloomberg-reported bidding contest between Seagate and Toshiba for TDK's magnetic-heads business — the only independent maker of the components — a deal that could be worth several billion dollars.
Memory stocks fell: Seagate -9% and Western Digital -7%, SK Hynix -6.5%, SanDisk -2.5%; the Roundhill memory ETF (DRAM) was down 3.5%.

Option Care Health soared 32.7% after drug distributor McKesson and private-equity firm Clayton Dubilier & Rice agreed to buy the infusion-therapy provider in a deal worth about $5.8 billion, including debt.
Moderna traded 6% lower and Novavax declined 10%, reversing some of the sharp gains made of late — despite those declines, Moderna remained more than 130% higher over the past three months.

chains.t: ③ Oil's Round Trip: Below $98 in the Morning, $100.58 at the Close
steps: The supply specifics: Saudi's East-West pipeline is back at 5.8M bpd (about 83% of capacity, the energy minister said), and Middle East flows ex-Iran topped pre-war levels on 4 of the last 7 days of September (Kpler/Vortexa)
The supply wave keeps rolling: the G7's 100M-barrel release is still flowing diesel-first
A domestic patch: Trump's executive order lets truckers and farmers use cheaper red-dyed diesel more broadly to bring down record-high fuel costs
The premium stays armed: traders keep watching Houthi attacks on Saudi targets and Hormuz tanker flows; PVM's John Evans: more crude getting through has 'dampened price fervour'
The close: Brent settles +0.26% at $100.58 (December basis); WTI +0.01% at $89.44
chains.d: Oil's round trip — under $98 to a $100.58 settle — was the day's second relief valve and its reminder: supply news can cool the barrel, but the war premium re-arms it by the close.

news.fact: Oil prices ended the day little changed: Brent crude traded 0.26% higher to settle at $100.58 a barrel; WTI futures rose 0.01% to $89.44.

Saudi Arabia's energy minister said oil pumped through the East-West Pipeline had reached 5.8 million barrels a day — about 83% of its 7 million bpd capacity — as of Tuesday morning, helping bypass the Strait of Hormuz.
Oil slipped as Middle East exports and the G7's stockpile release eased supply concerns.
Gulf oil flows excluding Iran averaged over 81% of pre-war levels in September, led by a recovery in Saudi exports, while Iranian exports fell to zero under a US blockade.

Oil prices ticked higher as tanker shipments through the Strait of Hormuz increased, but traders kept an eye on attacks by Iran-backed Houthi rebels on Saudi targets; both benchmarks had been comfortably lower Tuesday morning.
Trump signed an executive order to temporarily allow truckers and farmers to use cheaper red-dyed diesel more broadly, in an attempt to bring down record-high fuel costs.

chains.t: ④ The Relief Ledger: Bond Calm, Priced-Out October — and Wednesday's Test
steps: The calls get louder: Apollo's Slok sees yields peaking within a month; BCA calls Treasuries 'deeply oversold' with a 'tactical rally' ahead; JPMorgan is tactically bullish
The odds: October hike ~19% (from ~51% a week ago); December ~84% — the near-term Fed path is nearly priced out
Earnings optimism takes the handoff: LSEG sees +30.6% Q3 EPS growth (energy +114.7%, tech +66.5%); Lamb Weston +7.5% after lifting its full-year outlook; season opens next week with the banks
The gates: FOMC minutes Wednesday 2 pm ET; CPI Oct 14; the Oct 28 meeting — the ceiling is tested, not removed
The quiet signature: gold closed +0.7% at $4,187.10, bitcoin -0.2% — no panic anywhere in the cross-asset tape
chains.d: Four shock absorbers for Tuesday's records: a bond market that finally paused, an October hike nearly priced out, earnings expectations running hot, and a deal machine still buying.

news.fact: The sell-off in bonds appeared to abate, and several Wall Street analysts say the worst may be over: Apollo's Torsten Slok expects yields to peak within a month; BCA Research calls Treasuries 'deeply oversold' with a 'tactical rally' ahead; and JPMorgan is tactically bullish.
Markets priced a 19.4% probability of a second consecutive Fed hike this month, down from 50.9% a week ago, per CME's FedWatch tool.

Analysts expect S&P 500 companies to report 30.6% year-over-year earnings growth for the third quarter, led by an expected 114.7% jump in energy earnings and 66.5% in tech (LSEG); earnings season kicks off next week with the big banks.
Markets still price an ~84% probability of a rate increase in December even as October odds fade; the Fed publishes September's FOMC minutes Wednesday at 2 p.m. ET.
'We don't expect (the Fed) to do anything at the next meeting,' said Tim Ghriskey of Ingalls & Snyder. 'But I think they're in a gradual hiking cycle.'

chains.t: ⑤ The Internals Check: Broad Sectors, Thin Tails — and a Quiet Record
steps: Sector breadth was the week's widest: 10 of 11 green, led by utilities (+3.0%), with Health Care (-0.2%) the lone holdout
Advancers: NYSE 1.93-to-1, but the Nasdaq only 1.01-to-1 — the megacap-led narrowness persists under the record
New highs vs lows: S&P 23 vs 2; Nasdaq 61 vs 182 — the tail of the market is still being sold
Small caps lagged their larger-cap counterparts (Russell 2000 -0.6%); volume ran 16.50B shares against a 17.51B average — a quiet, orderly record
chains.d: The internals say 'record with an asterisk': broader sectors, but a Nasdaq barely positive on advancers and a small-cap tape still on the wrong side.

news.fact: All but health care among the 11 S&P sectors gained ground, with utilities leading the way; small caps lagged their larger-cap counterparts.
On the NYSE advancers outnumbered decliners 1.93-to-1; on the Nasdaq the ratio was just 1.01-to-1. The S&P 500 posted 23 new 52-week highs and 2 new lows; the Nasdaq, 61 highs and 182 lows.
Volume on US exchanges ran about 16.50 billion shares, versus a 17.51 billion average over the last 20 sessions.
Utilities was the top-performing S&P sector — up 2.4% with an hour to go — as Health Care became the only sector in the red, barely, with Moderna and Illumina both down about 6% at the time.

mtd.h: October, Four Sessions In: +2.19%, Two Records, and a Softening Ceiling
mtd.d: S&P 7,651.5 to 7,818.93 (+2.19% MTD): four sessions that ran the full range — fresh 2002 highs twice, then the first real retreat — closing with the index above 7,800 for the first time.
mtd.c1: Four sessions into October, the month has its first full arc: the ceiling held twice (the 10Y printed fresh 2002 highs on Oct 1 and Oct 5), then gave once — and the S&P is +2.19% MTD at 7,818.93, above 7,800 for the first time, with the Nasdaq +2.75% (two record closes) and the Dow +1.21%. The month's fuel: the post-payrolls dovish repricing (October hike odds down to ~19% from ~51% a week ago), a deal wave (PTC, RXO, Option Care), and AI's compounding — now led by power (Constellation's Google PPA). The tax: a 10Y that ends the window at 5.27% (-2bp MTD) after a 5.349% spike; WTI -1.1% as supply news met a re-arming premium; gold flat; the dollar +0.4% with the euro still pinned near 17-month lows. Beneath: Utilities (+4.4%) and Energy (+3.7%) lead sectors, Health (-0.8%) lags. Next gates: FOMC minutes (Wednesday), CPI (Oct 14) — then the earnings wave must validate the +30.6% Q3 consensus.
mtd.c4:
• October's verdict so far: dovish odds + deal tape + AI > the 10Y — but only while the 10Y stays under ~5.35%; the ceiling is tested, not removed.
  • Sector signature: inflation beneficiaries (Energy, Utilities) and growth (Tech) both bid; defensives and Health taxed — dispersion, not direction.
  • Gates: FOMC minutes (Wed 2 pm), CPI (Oct 14), the Oct 28 meeting — December (~84%) is where the hawkish risk sits.

qtd.d: 9/30 7,651.5 to 10/6 7,818.93 (+2.19% QTD): the quarter's opening week delivered two record closes, the 10Y's round trip from 5.29% to 5.35% and back to 5.27%, and a template built on dispersion.

ytd.h: The Bull Holds Into Q4: S&P +14.22% as the 10Y's +111bp Sets the Terms
ytd.d: S&P +14.22%, Nasdaq +18.75% (record), Dow +7.19% with four sessions of Q4 logged — AI and earnings carry; the 10Y's +111bp and an eighth month of war still tax the rest.
ytd.c1: Four sessions into Q4 and the year's base case is intact: the bull runs on AI capex and earnings proof, fighting the same two taxes — a 10Y up 111bp to 5.27% (2002 highs printed as recently as Monday) and oil up ~56% as the war grinds through its eighth month. The scoreboard: S&P +14.22%, Nasdaq +18.75% (record close), Dow +7.19%; underneath, Energy (+42.6%) leads and Consumer Discretionary (-6.4%) lags, with Utilities (-3.6%) still negative despite October's power bid. Tuesday added the year's newest theme — power as the AI bottleneck (Constellation/Google's nuclear PPA; Nvidia closing in on $6T) — and the memory complex's second supply scare in a week. December still prices ~84% for a hike; the Fed's minutes land Wednesday.
ytd.c4:
• The year's lesson holds into Q4: buy where earnings compound (AI infrastructure), rent where rates rule (long duration, the consumer).
  • Rates: the 10Y's +111bp is 2026's biggest tax — a confirmed Fed pause is the largest single bullish catalyst left this year.
  • New in Q4: power and memory supply are the AI trade's fault lines — bottlenecks are where the next repricing happens.
